_comment: Defects with no code home — tooling, environment, or a fault in a test file, which src-only scanning cannot see. A defect that DOES have a code home is declared with an @broken block beside the broken code instead, so deleting the code deletes the entry. Rendered into DEBT.md; do not edit that file.

entries.what: `pnpm typecheck` fails at the workspace level: four TS18048 errors, `'machine.seqs.move' is possibly 'undefined'` and the same for the `before`/`afterLoad` locals, under `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`. Pre-existing — confirmed by checking out `main` and running it there, where it fails identically. Found 2026-07-31 while verifying the invariants package, which typechecks clean itself.

Card Lab's state pills do not change the bench, so the layout audit measures ten cards EMPTY. Their real content — the case where a floor is most likely to be wrong — is never audited, while the sweep reports on all 43 as though coverage were uniform. Measured 2026-07-31 across the four-pitch sweep. This is what keeps `dev/card-floor-independent-of-size` at rung 4 rather than merely the sweep being manual.

Invariant B reports drift by POSITION, so the audit panel gives a count of drifting descendants rather than naming which element moved. A reader has to hunt for the culprit, which in practice means the finding is noted and not acted on.
entries.fix: Mitigated only in that the count is at least correct and ranks violations first. Real fix: report a stable path to the drifting node.

entries.what: The layout sweep runs at one viewport width. Media queries add no specificity and every desktop-width measurement sits above the breakpoints, so the entire class of narrow-viewport bugs — the one that produced 'fine on the dev server, broken on the printer' and cost four wrong diagnoses — is invisible to it by construction.

There is no oracle comparing a card's DECLARED natural size against its MEASURED floor. Invariants A and B both ask whether geometry is stable, and neither asks whether it is correct: a card whose declared size cannot contain its own content passes both while rendering clipped.

Five two-step controls armed with a raw createSignal instead of createArmed, so Escape reached none of them — firmware flash (M997), heater-fault reset, per-object cancel, filament delete, and save-to-machine. control/armed.ts meanwhile stated that Escape disarms EVERY armed control "including ones written later by someone who never read this file". Reading the code during the 2026-07-31 sweep found ONE of the five; the walking test found all five.
entries.fix: All five converted to createArmed. test/armed.test.ts now walks src and rejects any [armed, …] signal not produced by createArmed, naming file and line — red-checked, it failed on all five before the fix. Promotes control/escape-disarms from rung 5 to 6.

entries.what: Pause, Resume and Cancel were raw <button>s calling void sendCode(...) with no catch and no acknowledgement, so a rejected code or a blocking write guard left the operator believing a running print was paused or cancelled when nothing was sent. The last three buttons the 2026-07-22 audit left on raw elements, still unconverted 136 commits later.
entries.fix: Converted to GcodeButton, whose acknowledgement follows the connector PROMISE rather than the click. The job-toggle width reservation is kept, so Cancel still cannot slide under the pointer on a state change.
